title: The Distant Glasshouse
premise: Ivo Almeida has spent eleven years writing postcards to her mother at an address that burned down, a private ritual of everything she cannot say aloud. At her grandmother's funeral, a stranger named Beatriz greets the family as 'the Vasconcelos'—a name Ivo has never heard—and reveals that the matriarch's fortune, and the glasshouse where Ivo grew up, were built on a life lived under two identities. As Ivo investigates, she uncovers that her mother didn't die in the fire but fled it, choosing disappearance over inheritance, and that Beatriz is the daughter her grandmother left behind. When the glasshouse is scheduled for demolition and her father's health collapses, Ivo must finally send one postcard to a real address, forcing her family to answer the question they arranged themselves around: who was allowed to survive, and at what cost. The novel ends with Ivo refusing both the inheritance and the silence, keeping the glasshouse alive not as property but as a public garden bearing both names.
about_author: Mara Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters in a northern coastal town. She writes about families that keep their histories in sealed rooms.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We meet her ritual: postcards written to a burned address, filed by year in a shoebox, each cataloguing something unsaid. Her grandmother's funeral is tomorrow and she has packed nothing to wear. Emotional beat: controlled grief hiding a deeper avoidance.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the funeral, a woman in a green coat calls the family 'the Vasconcelos.' Ivo's father goes white; her aunt steers the stranger away. The glasshouse glints beyond the cemetery wall. Emotional beat: first crack in the family's careful surface.

chapters.title: What the Stone Says
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The headstone bears only 'Almeida,' yet the funeral register shows the green-coated woman signed 'B. Vasconcelos.' Ivo asks her aunt, who answers with a recipe instead of a name. Emotional beat: the itch of a question no one will touch.

chapters.title: Postcard 1,412
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with excerpts of her postcards. That night she writes to her dead mother as always, but for the first time asks a question: did you know her? Emotional beat: the ritual begins to fail her.

chapters.title: The Green Coat
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz watches the house from across the road, holding a photograph of two girls in a glasshouse. She has come to claim nothing, she tells herself. Emotional beat: longing disciplined into patience.

chapters.title: Aunt Odete's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Odete feeds her codfish cakes and warns her off 'cemetery strangers'—people who invent kinship at funerals. But her hands shake peeling garlic. Emotional beat: love expressed as obstruction.

chapters.title: The Deed
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sorting her grandmother's papers, Ivo finds the deed to the glasshouse made out to 'L. Vasconcelos, alias L. Almeida.' Her grandmother had two legal names. Emotional beat: vertigo—the ground of family history tilts.

chapters.title: Letters Not Mine
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz visits the town archive and finds letters addressed to her mother returned unopened for forty years, all in the same handwriting. Emotional beat: hope curdling into evidence.

chapters.title: Father's Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She confronts her father, Tomás, with the deed. He says only: 'Your grandmother paid for us to be nobody. Respect that.' Emotional beat: duty weaponized as kindness.

chapters.title: The Glasshouse at Night
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She breaks into the derelict glasshouse through a broken pane and finds a child's initials scratched inside a bench: B.V., beside her own mother's. Emotional beat: awe and dread entwined.

chapters.title: Two Girls, One Summer
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, grandmother Leonor's POV, 1962. Two half-sisters play in the glasshouse; only one will inherit the name that matters. Emotional beat: innocence before arrangement.

chapters.title: The Arrangement
chapters.summary: Leonor's POV, continuing. Their father decrees one daughter legitimate, one invisible. Leonor promises her sister she'll find a way around it. Emotional beat: a promise made in bad faith to fate.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A developer's notice appears on the glasshouse fence: thirty days. Ivo realizes the family let it decay deliberately—a monument allowed to rot. Emotional beat: urgency colliding with inherited passivity.

chapters.title: Coffee with a Stranger
chapters.summary: Ivo and Beatriz's alternating POVs. They finally speak; each tests the other, neither lies exactly. Beatriz shows the photograph. Emotional beat: cautious recognition between two keepers of halves.

chapters.title: Postcards Returned
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz reveals the archive letters—in her mother's hand, sent yearly to the burned address, mirroring Ivo's ritual. Two women wrote to ghosts across the same silence. Emotional beat: devastating symmetry.

chapters.title: The Fire, Version One
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. He remembers the fire as an accident, his mother's escape as grief-driven wandering. His memory is a shelter he built on purpose. Emotional beat: the comfort of not knowing.

chapters.title: The Fire, Version Two
chapters.summary: Odete's POV. Odete knows more: her mother set the fire herself, burning the documents that proved which daughter was legitimate. Emotional beat: guilt carried so long it feels like loyalty.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo tries the name 'Vasconcelos' aloud at dinner; her father leaves the table. Her aunt washes dishes that don't need washing. Emotional beat: the family's architecture of silence under load.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The developer offers the family money to walk away; Tomás wants to sign. Ivo stalls, buying time she doesn't know how to use. Emotional beat: complicity offered as relief.

chapters.title: Mother's Last Address
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the archive, Ivo finds a forwarding order her mother filed before disappearing—one real address, never followed. Emotional beat: terror that the question might actually be answerable.

chapters.title: The Road South
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Against Tomás's wishes, Ivo travels to the address with Beatriz. Road-trip intimacy; two women comparing wounds. Emotional beat: alliance forming out of shared orphanhood.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Story
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. An old caretaker remembers 'the quiet Vasconcelos girl' who came asking about the fire, then vanished inland. The trail warms and thins. Emotional beat: hope rationed carefully.

chapters.title: Hospital Light
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Tomás collapses; Ivo returns to a hospital room and a father suddenly willing to talk—or too weak not to. Emotional beat: fear softening into opening.

chapters.title: What Father Knew
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. He confesses: he found his mother's sister once, years ago, and turned away at her door because the family needed her to stay a ghost. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo writes the question the whole family arranged itself around—'Who did Grandmother choose?'—on a postcard and mails it to the last address. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Waiting Room
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. While Tomás worsens, Beatriz and Ivo wait together; Beatriz admits she came hoping for money and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: honesty as penance.

chapters.title: Reply, Forwarded Twice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. An envelope arrives, forwarded twice, containing no letter—only a pressed flower from a glasshouse rose and a new address. Emotional beat: trembling elation.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Left
chapters.summary: Ivo and Beatriz travel again. At a coastal town they find an old woman who is not Ivo's mother—but her mother's cousin, keeper of the true story. Emotional beat: revelation deferred, deepened.

chapters.title: The True Ledger
chapters.summary: Cousin Rosa's POV. Rosa tells all: Leonor didn't flee the fire—she was sent away to protect the forged legitimacy, and chose exile over exposing her sister. Emotional beat: the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: Mother Is Alive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Rosa gives the final address. Ivo's hands shake so badly she can't hold the paper. Eleven years of postcards to a dead woman—and her mother lives. Emotional beat: fury and joy indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo demands the family go to her mother; Tomás refuses—'She chose this'; Odete wavers. Demolition is now five days away. Emotional beat: the family fracture becomes open war.

chapters.title: Postcard 1,500
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo writes her mother a real postcard to a real address and cannot mail it—what do you say after eleven years of practice? Emotional beat: paralysis at the threshold of forgiveness.

chapters.title: Beatriz Decides
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz, done waiting, mails Ivo's postcard herself and signs her own name beneath it. Emotional beat: love acting where duty froze.

chapters.title: The Last Day of the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Demolition morning: bulldozers at the gate, the family assembled, and a taxi pulling up with a small, gray-haired woman inside. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Who Was Allowed to Survive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Mother and daughters face each other among the glass panes. No absolution comes easily; the mother does not apologize, only explains, and Ivo must decide what explanation is worth. Emotional beat: climax—grief meeting its object.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The family must sign or refuse the developer. Ivo refuses her share publicly; Odete follows; Tomás, from his hospital bed, sends a proxy vote against. The sale dies. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as refusal.

chapters.title: Both Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The glasshouse is transferred to a land trust under both names—Almeida and Vasconcelos—to become a public winter garden. Beatriz plants the first bed. Emotional beat: mourning converted into structure.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Bloom
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Winter opens in the restored glasshouse; townspeople wander among blooming roses that shouldn't survive the season but do. Emotional beat: fragile, earned warmth.

chapters.title: The Empty Shoebox
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reads her 1,500 postcards one last time, then burns them in the glasshouse stove—except the last one, which her mother finally answered. Emotional beat: release without forgetting.

chapters.title: Everything Said
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing. Spring: Ivo writes one final postcard—not to a ghost, but to Beatriz, next door, about dinner. Some things are said simply now. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
